questions.key_step: Factor out the largest term; remaining ratios die off.
questions.justification: Standard 'max-term' trick for sums of powers; two short steps.

questions.key_step: Reduce to [x]-[2x]=7 and test existence at piece boundaries.
questions.justification: Several GIF pieces to check but routine; like a Main-type GIF limit.

questions.key_step: Group the numerator in threes and rationalise.
questions.justification: Routine chain: pattern sum, conjugate, leading terms.

questions.key_step: Use q=-4-2p to see the argument is (x-2p)^2, then the side from which f approaches 1/2.
questions.justification: Hidden perfect square plus the floor of a value approached from below is a non-routine subtlety.

questions.key_step: Evaluate h on both sides: h(-k)=h(k)=-1.
questions.justification: Few steps with signum/GIF; routine.

questions.key_step: (a+b)^6+(a-b)^6 keeps even terms; compare leading powers.
questions.justification: Heavy but routine expansion; or dominant-term shortcut.

questions.key_step: Rationalise to telescope the AP sum.
questions.justification: One telescoping trick, then a short limit.

questions.key_step: Sandwich the product between nth powers of the smallest and largest factors.
questions.justification: Single idea (all factors <1) applied once.

questions.key_step: Reduce to standard limits sin kx/kx and ln(1+kx)/kx.
questions.justification: Direct application of standard limits.

questions.key_step: x^2+bx+a=a(1-alpha x)(1-beta x) gives the 1-cos u / u^2 form.
questions.justification: Non-obvious link between the roots of ax^2+bx+1 and x^2+bx+a, then algebra; two ideas linked.

questions.key_step: Series expansion; first-order coefficient must vanish.
questions.justification: Routine series expansion with two conditions.

questions.key_step: Double rationalisation for a, single for b.
questions.justification: Routine conjugate steps, a little long.

questions.key_step: Vanishing of constant and x coefficients, x^2 coefficient given.
questions.justification: Standard series expansion, three short conditions.

questions.key_step: Even function; on the right |sin x|=sin x and use standard limits.
questions.justification: Few routine steps.

questions.key_step: Monotonicity squeezes f(5x)/f(x) from above 1; floor of a small positive number is 0.
questions.justification: Abstract function, an idea students seldom practise (floor of a quantity tending to 1 from above).

questions.key_step: Undo f three times with parity checks; then trivial limit.
questions.justification: Routine but needs care with parity.

questions.key_step: Series expansion with three constants and a x^3 coefficient condition.
questions.justification: Numerical answer; three equations from series, a slip changes the result; no options.

questions.key_step: Left side has {x}->1-, right side {x}->0+; different local analysis for each side.
questions.justification: Two different one-sided computations with inverse trig and fractional part; numerical format.

questions.key_step: Identify the correct general term (k^2-k)(n-k); leading power n^4 of each sum.
questions.justification: Needs the series structure recognised and several power sums; leading-term logic.

questions.key_step: Eliminate y; cancel (c-1); circle through a point.
questions.justification: Three routine stages (intersection, limit, circle) with no insight.

questions.key_step: Write as e^{...}, factor e, standard limits.
questions.justification: 1^inf-type expansion; routine but needs second-order care.

questions.key_step: 0/0 form; differentiate numerator and denominator.
questions.justification: Routine L'Hospital with fractional powers; identify m, n.

questions.key_step: 1/a is a root of 2+x-2x^2, giving the 1-cos u / u^2 form; then surd algebra.
questions.justification: Hidden factorisation plus heavy surd arithmetic with no options to check against.

questions.key_step: Evaluate two limits, then Vieta.
questions.justification: Two standard limits, then Vieta with surds; numerical format.
